Indicator_Name: Total UK territorial GHG emissions
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: Climate Change Act 2008, s.1 & s.4; Carbon Budgets 4–7
Data_Source: DESNZ UK GHG Inventory (provisional and final)
Climate_Rationale: UK GHG inventory uses activity data × emission factors; temperature marginally affects heating demand and agricultural CH4/N2O, but inventory is not formally weather-adjusted at source.
Framework_Classification: Role: Overarching target; Benchmark: CB4: ≤1,950 MtCO₂e (2023–27); CB5: ≤1,725 MtCO₂e (2028–32); CB6: ≤965 MtCO₂e (2033–37); Net Zero by 2050; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: UK GHG emissions (excluding international aviation & shipping)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: Paris Agreement UK NDC; Climate Change Act 2008
Data_Source: DESNZ UK GHG Inventory
Climate_Rationale: As above — same inventory methodology excluding international aviation/shipping.
Framework_Classification: Role: Overarching target; Benchmark: NDC: −68% by 2030 vs 1990; −81% by 2035 vs 1990; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Temperature-adjusted buildings sector emissions
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Mitigation Monitoring Framework (June 2025, updated June 2026) – Buildings; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: DESNZ UK GHG Inventory + CCC temperature adjustment
Climate_Rationale: CCC explicitly applies a temperature adjustment (Heating Degree Day regression) to buildings emissions to remove weather effects before assessing policy progress; weather data are a direct, formal input.
Framework_Classification: Role: Emissions target; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway; CBGDP buildings pathway (October 2025), which reduces buildings emissions more slowly than the CBDP 2023 it replaced; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Consumption-based GHG emissions (imports)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Monitoring Framework 2025 – wider emissions monitoring
Data_Source: Defra consumption emissions statistics
Climate_Rationale: Consumption-based emissions from MRIO input-output tables; climate is not a direct input but extreme weather events can affect production in global supply chains.
Framework_Classification: Role: Overarching target; Benchmark: No statutory target; monitored vs historical trend; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Share of electricity from renewable & low-carbon sources
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Monitoring Framework 2025 – Electricity supply; Clean Power 2030 Action Plan; Net Zero Strategy
Data_Source: National Energy System Operator (NESO) / Elexon / DESNZ
Climate_Rationale: Renewable and low-carbon share of generation is moved strongly by wind, solar and rainfall, a known significant confounder, but it is metered generation and weather is not an input (Legend 2, rule D).
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: Clean power by 2030 (GB); 50 GW offshore wind by 2030; 70 GW solar by 2035; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Installed offshore wind capacity
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.7; Clean Power 2030 Action Plan; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: DESNZ Energy Trends; Renewable UK
Climate_Rationale: Installed offshore wind capacity from DESNZ/RenewableUK records; capacity is a static installed figure unaffected by weather.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: Clean Power 2030 Action Plan: 43-50 GW of offshore wind by 2030. 16.6 GW installed at end-2025 (0.7 GW added in the year); the CCC assesses the current pipeline as delivering about 32 GW by 2030, so 5.3-6.7 GW average annual deployment is needed to close the gap. AR7 contracted a record 8.2 GW fixed and 0.2 GW floating.; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Installed onshore wind capacity
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Balanced Pathway / Seventh Carbon Budget
Data_Source: DESNZ Energy Trends; Renewable UK
Climate_Rationale: Installed onshore wind capacity — as above.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: 27–29 GW by 2030 (CCC Balanced Pathway); CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Installed solar PV capacity
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.7; Clean Power 2030 Action Plan; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: DESNZ Energy Trends; Solar Energy UK

Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: Clean Power 2030 Action Plan: 45-47 GW of solar PV by 2030 - a GOVERNMENT ambition, not a CCC pathway figure as this row previously recorded. 21.7 GW installed at end-2025, with 2.8 GW added in 2025, the highest annual deployment since 2015. The 70 GW by 2035 figure came from the earlier Net Zero Strategy and is not the current benchmark.; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Nuclear generation capacity (operational)

Indicator_Name: Gas-fired power generation (unabated)

Source_Reference: Clean Power 2030 Action Plan; CCC Monitoring Framework
Data_Source: DESNZ Energy Trends

Indicator_Name: Battery storage and long-duration energy storage capacity

Indicator_Name: Contracts for Difference (CfD) auction capacity secured
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.7; Clean Power 2030 Action Plan; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025

Framework_Classification: Role: Demand / activity; Benchmark: No statutory demand target; monitored vs CCC pathway; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Annual heat pump installations (residential)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.3, §4.3.3; Warm Homes Plan 2025; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: MCS certification data; DESNZ Boiler Upgrade Scheme statistics
Climate_Rationale: Heat pump installations from MCS certification data; no climate data. (Heat pump performance varies with outdoor temperature, but the indicator counts installations.)
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: Warm Homes Plan: 450,000 heat pump installations per year UK-wide by 2030, of which ~250,000 retrofit; the CCC states installation rates must exceed this to deliver the CBGDP emissions reductions. CCC Balanced Pathway: retrofit at roughly twice the Warm Homes Plan level, reaching ~1.4 million/year by 2035. (Superseded: the Heat and Buildings Strategy aim of 600,000/year by 2028.); CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Homes upgraded to EPC band C or above
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §4.3.3; Warm Homes Plan 2025; planned MEES legislation (not yet enacted)
Data_Source: MHCLG / Valuation Office EPC register
Climate_Rationale: EPC ratings from VOA/MHCLG register; static rating, no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: Planned Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards: private rented homes to EPC C on two EPC metrics by 2030 (~1.8 million homes); social rented homes to EPC C on one metric by 2030 and two metrics by 2039 (~1.1 million by 2030, ~2.9 million by 2039). The Heat and Buildings Strategy aim of all homes EPC C by 2035 is no longer government policy.; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Number of properties insulated (loft, cavity wall, solid wall)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.3, §4.3.3; Warm Homes Plan 2025. ECO4 closed — the scheme cited in the previous benchmark no longer exists
Data_Source: DESNZ Energy Company Obligation (ECO) statistics
Climate_Rationale: Insulation installations from ECO scheme records; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: No quantified government insulation target. The CCC tracks the proportion of homes with cavity wall insulation and assesses it on track. The Energy Company Obligation, which delivered about a third of the retrofit market over three years, has closed with no replacement; planned MEES are expected to drive efficiency improvements in ~1.8 million private rented and ~1.1 million social rented homes by 2030.; CCC key indicator: No

Source_Reference: CCC Mitigation Monitoring Framework (June 2025, updated June 2026) – Buildings; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: DESNZ UK GHG Inventory
Climate_Rationale: Unadjusted residential emissions from the DESNZ inventory; cold winters move heating emissions but weather is not an input to this series. The temperature-adjusted series is held separately at [IND-C-003] (Legend 1, rule C).
Framework_Classification: Role: Emissions target; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway; CBGDP buildings pathway (October 2025), which reduces buildings emissions more slowly than the CBDP 2023 it replaced; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Average home Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) rating
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: Heat and Buildings Strategy 2021
Data_Source: MHCLG / VOA EPC register
Climate_Rationale: EPC rating from SAP assessment methodology; SAP uses standard heating assumptions not actual weather.
Framework_Classification: Role: Energy efficiency; Benchmark: All homes EPC C by 2035; SAP improvement benchmarks; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Non-residential buildings energy intensity
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.3, §4.3.3; CCC Mitigation Monitoring Framework (June 2025, updated June 2026) – Buildings; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: DESNZ Energy Consumption in the UK (ECUK)
Climate_Rationale: Non-residential building energy intensity from ECUK; energy use is affected by weather (heating/cooling) but ECUK does not formally weather-adjust this indicator.
Framework_Classification: Role: Energy efficiency; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway; CBGDP buildings pathway (October 2025). No dedicated funding for the public estate since the Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme closed, and the non-residential MEES uplift from EPC E to EPC B by 2030, first consulted on in 2019, remains unconfirmed.; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Industrial energy consumption per unit output (energy intensity)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.5, §4.3.5; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: DESNZ Energy Consumption in the UK (ECUK)
Climate_Rationale: Industrial energy per unit output from ECUK; process energy is largely weather-independent (Legend 1, rules C and G; aligned with [IND-C-027], [IND-C-055]).
Framework_Classification: Role: Energy efficiency; Benchmark: The CBGDP sets no industrial energy-intensity target. It makes ELECTRIFICATION the primary route to industrial decarbonisation, with a larger role than the CBDP 2023 gave it. CCC Balanced Pathway: electricity reaches 36% of industrial energy demand by 2030, against 27% in 2024 (down from 28% in 2023). The industrial electricity-to-gas price ratio, about 4:1 against the roughly 3:1 needed for industrial heat pumps, is the binding constraint.; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Industrial GHG emissions
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Monitoring Framework 2025 – Industry; Industrial Decarbonisation Strategy 2021
Data_Source: DESNZ UK GHG Inventory
Climate_Rationale: Industrial GHG emissions from inventory; temperature marginally affects fuel use in some sectors but inventory is not formally weather-adjusted.
Framework_Classification: Role: Emissions target; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway; ~71% reduction by 2035 vs 2019; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) capacity operational (industrial CCUS)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CBGDP Section 14 Report (DESNZ, 29 October 2025, updated 23 June 2026); CBGDP technical annex; CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament §4.3.5
Data_Source: DESNZ / CCUS programme reports
Climate_Rationale: Industrial CCS capacity from DESNZ project pipeline; operational capture statistics may vary with plant output (some weather-sensitive) but the indicator tracks installed capacity.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: CBGDP: the Track-1 clusters enable storage capacity of up to 4 MtCO2/year at the East Coast Cluster and 4.5 MtCO2/year at HyNet at full network utilisation, about 8.5 MtCO2/year combined, with £9.4 billion of capital allocated at Spending Review 2025 to fill it. East Coast reached financial close in December 2024 and HyNet transport and storage in April 2025; Protos and Padeswood capture projects reached FID in September 2025. Track-2 (Acorn, Viking) has development funding with a final investment decision due later this Parliament, and gas-terminal CCUS savings are expected from 2034. The CBGDP sets NO economy-wide CCUS capacity target for 2030: the 20-30 MtCO2/year figure in the previous benchmark came from the Net Zero Strategy 2021 and is not restated.; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Low-carbon hydrogen production capacity
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CBGDP Section 14 Report (DESNZ, 29 October 2025, updated 23 June 2026) paras 26, 88; CBGDP technical annex paras 86-91; UK Hydrogen Strategy 2021 (superseded figure)
Data_Source: DESNZ Hydrogen production statistics
Climate_Rationale: Hydrogen production capacity from DESNZ statistics; installed electrolyser capacity is not weather-dependent.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: The CBGDP sets NO hydrogen production capacity target. Capacity is derived from modelled demand in the industry, power and transport sectors on the assumption that supply always equals demand, with CCUS-enabled (blue) plants at a 90% load factor and electrolytic (green) at 60%. Delivery runs through allocation rounds: HAR1 (11 projects funded), HAR2 (27 projects shortlisted April 2025), HAR3 to launch by 2026 and HAR4 from 2028; two CCUS-enabled projects in the East Coast and HyNet clusters could add up to 1 GW. A new Hydrogen Strategy is in preparation to set out the scale government envisages. The 10 GW by 2030 in the previous benchmark comes from the UK Hydrogen Strategy 2021 and is not restated in the CBGDP.; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Industrial fuel switching to low-carbon alternatives
Units_Measure: % of industrial energy from low-carbon fuels
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: Industrial Decarbonisation Strategy 2021; CCC Monitoring Framework
Data_Source: DESNZ Energy Consumption in the UK (ECUK)
Climate_Rationale: Industrial fuel switching share from ECUK; no direct climate data.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway: significant electrification and hydrogen by 2030s; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Livestock numbers (cattle and sheep)

Source_Reference: CCC Monitoring Framework 2025 – Agriculture; Sixth & Seventh Carbon Budgets
Data_Source: Defra June Survey of Agriculture and Horticulture
Climate_Rationale: Livestock numbers from June Agricultural Survey; numbers are not directly weather-driven but drought/flooding affect fodder availability and may affect herd management.
Framework_Classification: Role: Demand / activity; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway: ~20% reduction by 2035 vs 2019 baseline; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Agricultural GHG emissions
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.4; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: DESNZ UK GHG Inventory
Climate_Rationale: Agricultural GHG emissions include N2O from soils and CH4 from enteric fermentation; soil N2O is strongly temperature and moisture dependent; IPCC methodology uses climate-informed emission factors.
Framework_Classification: Role: Emissions target; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway; CBGDP agriculture and land use pathway (October 2025). The Government has set no pathway or target for cattle and sheep numbers or for meat consumption. Both are currently running AHEAD of the Balanced Pathway without direct policy: cattle and sheep numbers fell about 1% and 2% in 2025 to their lowest since 1990, and household beef and lamb purchases fell 5%.; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Peatland restoration area (upland and lowland)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.4; UK and devolved administration peatland commitments; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: Natural England / Defra peatland monitoring
Climate_Rationale: Peatland restoration area from scheme records; no climate data in the area metric (though peat carbon flux monitoring uses temperature/rainfall data).
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: Combined peatland restoration ambition of the UK Government, the Northern Ireland Executive, the Scottish Government and the Welsh Government. 21,400 hectares restored across the UK in 2025, up 26% and surpassing the combined 2026 ambition; rates have more than tripled since 2020, with Scotland delivering 70% of the total. England, Wales and Northern Ireland figures are likely underestimates - England counts only the Nature for Climate Peatland Grant Scheme.; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Tree planting rate (new woodland creation)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.4; Forestry Statistics 2025; devolved planting targets; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: Forestry Commission woodland statistics
Climate_Rationale: Tree planting area from Forestry Commission records; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: Combined UK woodland creation ambition, which requires reaching annual rates last seen in the late 1980s by 2030. 15,600 hectares planted UK-wide in 2024/25, DOWN 25% on the previous year, driven by a 44% fall in Scotland following funding cuts; Scotland still delivered 54% of UK planting and has a new target of 18,000 ha/year by 2030. England reached 5,770 hectares, its highest since 2003.; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Land use change (net change in woodland and peatland cover)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Monitoring Framework 2025 – Agriculture & land use
Data_Source: Forest Research / Natural England / Defra LULUCF statistics
Climate_Rationale: Net change in woodland and peatland cover from inventory mapping; climate is a long-run driver but no climate data enter the area calculation (Legend 1, rule B).
Framework_Classification: Role: Enabling / enabler; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway for LULUCF sink growth; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Agricultural nitrogen use efficiency
Units_Measure: kg N applied per tonne output (index)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CBGDP Section 14 Report (DESNZ, 29 October 2025, updated 23 June 2026) Nutrient Management and Advice & Guidance policy lines; CBGDP technical annex; CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (no corresponding indicator)
Data_Source: Defra British Survey of Fertiliser Practice (BSFP)
Climate_Rationale: Agricultural nitrogen efficiency from BSFP; fertiliser application varies with growing conditions (weather-driven) but the indicator uses survey data without formal weather adjustment.
Framework_Classification: Role: Energy efficiency; Benchmark: The CBGDP sets NO quantified fertiliser or nitrogen-use-efficiency target. It addresses agricultural nitrous oxide through named advice-and-guidance policies with market-led uptake: agronomist-led nutrient management plans to avoid nitrogen applied in excess, precision farming using machine guidance and variable-rate nitrogen application technology, grass and herbal leys in arable rotations, clover at 20% or more of mixed grassland, and analysis of slurry nitrogen content before application. The technical annex carries no fertiliser or nitrogen quantification, and the CCC 2026 progress report has no corresponding indicator.; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Uptake of sustainable farming practices (SFI / agri-environment scheme area)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Progress in reducing emissions 2026 report to Parliament (24 June 2026) §3.2.4, §4.3.4; Carbon Budget and Growth Delivery Plan 2025
Data_Source: Defra agri-environment statistics
Climate_Rationale: SFI/agri-environment scheme area from administrative records; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Role: Deployment / uptake; Benchmark: No quantified uptake target. England’s Sustainable Farming Incentive is to reopen in June 2026 and a 25-year Farming Roadmap is expected during 2026; all four UK nations now have successor agri-environment schemes in place following the Common Agricultural Policy. The CCC notes these present the opportunity to incentivise emissions-reducing practices but that long-term funding and policy certainty are required.; CCC key indicator: No

Indicator_Name: Aviation passenger demand
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: CCC Monitoring Framework 2025 – Aviation; Jet Zero Strategy 2022
Data_Source: Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) statistics
Climate_Rationale: Aviation passenger demand from CAA statistics; extreme weather causes temporary flight disruptions but annual demand figures are not weather-adjusted.
Framework_Classification: Role: Demand / activity; Benchmark: CCC Balanced Pathway: demand not to exceed ~2019 levels significantly; CCC key indicator: Yes

Indicator_Name: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) blend rate

Indicator_Name: Waste sector GHG emissions (landfill + other)
Policy_Goal: UK Climate Change Act 2008 carbon budgets; Carbon Budget Delivery Plan 2023; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity

Indicator_Name: Energy productivity (GDP per unit of energy consumed)

The CBGDP addresses energy demand through sectoral policy lines - industrial energy efficiency (policy 108) and domestic energy efficiency - rather than an economy-wide demand or productivity target.; CCC key indicator: No

Source_Reference: CCC Monitoring Framework 2025 – Agriculture & Land Use sector
Data_Source: NAEI (DESNZ)

Source_Reference: CCC Monitoring Framework 2025 – Agriculture & Land Use sector
Data_Source: NAEI (DESNZ)
